mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of an object placed 30 cm in front of the lens. The image is formed 60 cm on the other side of the lens. Using the lens formula with the Cartesian sign convention, what is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens, object distance u = -30 cm (real object) and image distance v = +60 cm (real image). The lens formula is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Substituting, 1/f = 1/60 - (-1/30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20, so f = 20 cm. Option B is correct.

mcqs.question: A concave lens forms a virtual image 10 cm behind the lens when an object is placed 20 cm in front of it. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave lens, both object and image distances are taken as negative: u = -20 cm, v = -10 cm. Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u = 1/(-10) - 1/(-20) = -0.1 + 0.05 = -0.05. Hence f = -20 cm. Option B is correct.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms an image 24 cm on the opposite side of the lens when the object is placed 12 cm in front of it. What is the linear magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Magnification m = v/u. With Cartesian sign convention, u = -12 cm, v = +24 cm, so m = 24/(-12) = -2. The negative sign indicates an inverted image. Option B is correct. Many students forget the sign and answer 2, which is a common misconception.

mcqs.question: The power of a thin lens is defined as:

options.A: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in metres
options.B: Its focal length measured in centimetres
options.C: The product of its object and image distances
options.D: The ratio of image height to object height

mcqs.answer: The reciprocal of its focal length measured in metres
mcqs.explanation: Lens power P (in dioptres) is defined as P = 1/f, where f is the focal length in metres. This definition allows easy addition of powers for lenses in contact. Hence option A is correct.

mcqs.question: Lens A has a focal length of 0.20 m, and Lens B has a focal length of -0.50 m. Which lens has the greater optical power (in dioptres)?

options.C: Both have the same magnitude of power
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the lens material

mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f. For Lens A, P = 1/0.20 = +5 D. For Lens B, P = 1/(-0.50) = -2 D. The magnitude of power of Lens A (5 D) is greater than that of Lens B (2 D). Therefore, Lens A has the greater optical power. Option A is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: A converging lens of power +3 D is placed in contact with a diverging lens of power -2 D. What is the focal length of the combined lens system?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add: P_total = +3 D + (-2 D) = +1 D. The focal length f_total = 1/P_total = 1/1 D = 1 m. Hence the combined system has a focal length of 1 metre. Option B is correct.

mcqs.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the lens formula using the Cartesian sign convention?
mcqs.explanation: With the Cartesian sign convention, object distance u is taken negative for real objects, while image distance v is positive for real images and negative for virtual images. The lens formula is therefore 1/f = 1/v - 1/u. Option B is the correct representation.

mcqs.question: According to the Cartesian sign convention, the object distance (u) for a real object placed in front of a lens is:

options.D: Depends on the type of lens

mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured against the direction of incident light are taken as negative. For a real object placed in front of a lens, the incident light travels from the object towards the lens, so the object distance u is negative. Hence option B is correct.
